quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is harder because you cannot see as well. It is harder to judge speed, distance, and hazards. Keep more space between your car and the car in front of you. This gives you time to stop if they stop suddenly. Use your headlights correctly at night.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, every vehicle has blind spots you cannot see. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: What should you do when a traffic signal is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop unless a police officer is directing traffic. Look both ways and yield the right-of-way before entering.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than regular cars. A car going 55 mph can stop in about 400 feet. A large truck going 55 mph needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, you can block traffic when you drive too slowly.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you can block traffic when you drive too slowly.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It makes you less alert, harder to focus, slower to react, and less coordinated.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down, move it as far off the road as possible. All four wheels should be off the main road.

questions.question: Why should you clean the inside of your windows if someone has been smoking?

options.text: Smoking causes a film to build up on the glass inside your vehicle.
Dust tends to settle on the insides of car windows.
The stale smell can be distracting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Smoking causes a film to build up on the glass inside your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smoking leaves a film on windows inside your car. Keep your windows clean, especially if someone has smoked in the vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes going the same direction will soon combine into one lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Falling rocks
Trucks use second gear
Steep hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a steep hill is ahead. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve ahead.
Drive no slower than 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Approach the upcoming curve at 35 mph or slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the upcoming curve at 35 mph or slower.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions just ahead. Speed advisory signs tell you the safe speed to drive.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the center of the roadway.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road if an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road so you can stay in your lane. Do not flash your bright lights in response.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to skid, do not use the brakes. Keep steering until the vehicle is under your control again and moving safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions just ahead. This sign tells you to be ready for traffic merging from the right.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, creating a hazard. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and step on the brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle merges in front of you too closely, take your foot off the accelerator. This creates space between you and the vehicle ahead without slamming on the brakes or swerving into another lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because drivers behind you may become frustrated and make unsafe moves to pass you. It is safest to drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.
You signal your intention for three seconds.
You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed. One way to check is to look in your rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights, you have enough room to return to your lane.

questions.question: You should not start across an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.
Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even if the light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. If you block the intersection, you can be cited.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Side road.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that the road becomes slippery when wet and you should drive carefully.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This helps other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots. The driver cannot see your car if you are directly behind the truck. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: An intersection.
A road curve.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign alerts drivers to be ready for a side road that intersects ahead.

questions.question: When following which vehicle should you allow extra space in front of your car?

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes suddenly.

questions.question: You see this sign for a railroad crossing without signals. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep a steady speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be ready to stop if a train is coming. Never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean about passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Your car's rear end starts skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This helps straighten out your vehicle.
